mission: Find movies and series that create a strong need to understand an impossible situation, phenomenon, organism, experiment, system, or reality-bending rule set. Discovery and concept escalation matter more than raw action.

strong_positive_signals.signal: Scientists actively investigating an unexplained or impossible phenomenon
Biology, genetics, mutation, alien organisms, ecology, parasites, evolution or unusual physiology
Unknown phenomenon whose rules are discovered through observation, testing or deduction
High-concept premise that keeps revealing new implications instead of stopping at one gimmick
Scientific experiments or technologies with unexpected consequences
Reality distortion, time anomalies, memory anomalies or consciousness manipulation
Artificial systems, games, facilities or social experiments whose hidden rules/purpose must be discovered
Suspense driven by needing to know what is actually happening
Conspiracies or secret research programs connected to the central phenomenon

negative_signals.signal: Straightforward monster/creature escape after the threat is revealed
Generic slasher, torture or psychological horror where the science/mystery is secondary
Space opera, franchise lore, military spectacle or action-first sci-fi with little investigation
Slow pacing where the movie withholds information without providing meaningful discoveries
Sequel or remake that mostly repeats an already-seen concept without a substantial new idea
Mystery whose payoff is primarily symbolic/ambiguous and not supported by ongoing discoveries

automation_rules.past_24h_definition: Only items with added_by=daily-automation and added_at within the last 24 hours.

principles.descriptive_only: A DNA value describes how strongly a property exists in a TITLE. It never states whether that property is desirable. Desirability lives only in dna_baseline and dna_guardrails.
principles.unknown_is_not_zero: Missing or null means UNKNOWN, never 'definitely absent'. Never substitute 0.
principles.unknown_never_satisfies: A threshold comparison against an unknown value is false in both directions. Unknown can never satisfy a positive or a negative test.
principles.unknown_is_not_safe: Unknown must not be read as 'passes the guardrail'. An item is not DNA-score-eligible unless every dimension referenced ANYWHERE in dna_guardrails is known - hard_exclusion, combination all_of and combination any_of alike. See dna_baseline.completeness_defaults.required_known_dimensions.
principles.independent_dimensions: creature_threat and survival_chase are separate information and must never be combined, averaged or substituted for one another, here or in any downstream consumer. The same holds for action_density and action_intensity: action_density is HOW MUCH of the runtime contains action, action_intensity is HOW HARD that action hits WHEN it occurs. Neither may be derived from the other, from a trailer, from pace_speed or from a genre label, and action_density requires whole-runtime or whole-season structural evidence. HISTORY, NOW CLOSED: the MG-7 shape migration introduced action_density as null on every record that existed at the time, and MG-7.2 then backfilled the complete 127-title legacy set. Those records now carry researched action_density AND action_intensity re-researched under the corrected peak-force rubric; no legacy backlog remains. A current accepted discovery MUST carry known integer values for BOTH dimensions. null still means unknown to the generic engine, and unknown is never zero, so an unmeasured value can never satisfy a gate or dodge a guardrail - but it is no longer an acceptable state for a completed Sci-Fi DNA Match record.

dna_dimensions.tag_registry_note: Controlled descriptive DNA tags. This vocabulary is CLOSED: item.dna_tags may contain only values from this array. dna_baseline.description: The desired CONTENT universe expressed on the DNA scale. Stable baseline. Accumulated user feedback is NEVER merged into this section.
dna_baseline.scale_note: Weights are commensurate with strong_positive_signals and negative_signals, in the range -40..40.
dna_baseline.unweighted_note: These six carry no linear baseline weight, and each for its own reason. pace_speed is meaningful only in combination (see dna_guardrails.combination.slow_without_discovery). space_opera, superhero and comic_book_universe are handled entirely by dna_guardrails so that a descriptive measurement is never confused with a policy decision. action_density and action_intensity are unweighted BY CALIBRATION, not because they are unmeasured: the baseline is a normalised weighted average, so a positive weight on a dimension the corpus scores low on behaves as a new requirement rather than a bonus - measured over the completed 127-title set, a positive action_density weight would have raised only the 19 lowest-scoring titles and lowered the other 95, and a negative action_intensity weight penalised titles purely for having forceful sequences. BOTH ARE REQUIRED-KNOWN AND FULLY RESEARCHED. action_density is referenced by dna_guardrails.combination.action_first_without_investigation and by the three action archetypes; sustained action earns its advantage there, through the archetype path, never through the linear average. weights and unweighted are disjoint and their union is exactly the 28 registry ids.

completeness_defaults.note: Baseline DNA score-eligibility. An item must satisfy ALL THREE conditions to be scored by the DNA path. required_known_dimensions must contain every dimension referenced ANYWHERE in dna_guardrails - hard_exclusion, combination all_of and combination any_of - so that an item can never pass a structural guardrail or dodge a combination penalty merely because the relevant dimension is unknown. It MAY be stricter than that minimum: product-level research completeness is a separate concern from the guardrail floor, and action_intensity is required-known even though no guardrail references it, because a discovery that has not measured how hard its action hits is not finished. An ineligible item is NOT excluded and NOT penalised by DNA; it falls back to the existing stable baseline ranking path until enrichment fills the missing values. Individual catalog rows may override these defaults in config/catalogs.json at F2-8, but may never remove a guardrail-referenced dimension from the required set.

dna_baseline.archetype_note: Scoring takes the BEST-matching archetype, never an average across them. Averaging distinct interests produces a mediocre midpoint and erases exactly the clusters this profile exists to find. requires_mode is mandatory on every archetype and has no default: 'all' means every entry in requires must hold, 'any' means at least one must hold. An archetype whose requires cannot be evaluated because the referenced dimensions are unknown simply does not match. The three action archetypes added at MG-7.3 are the ONLY route by which sustained action improves a general DNA Match score, and each requires action_density >= 5 TOGETHER WITH real Sci-Fi substance - investigation, rule discovery, or concept escalation plus mystery. None rewards density alone, and because scoring takes the single best-matching archetype rather than a sum, action flavours cannot stack. Consumed by build-site.mjs at F2-8; unused in F2-6.

dna_guardrails.description: Policy applied to descriptive DNA measurements. Not learnable away by ordinary feedback; changing these requires a deliberate edit of this file.
dna_guardrails.structural_note: Judge superhero, comic_book_universe and space_opera by story identity - costumed or superpowered hero structure, cinematic-universe-first storytelling, saga or war framing - not by franchise name.
dna_guardrails.evaluation_note: Guardrails are evaluated only for items that are DNA-score-eligible under dna_baseline.completeness_defaults. A condition whose dimension is unknown/null evaluates FALSE. A combination guardrail fires if and only if EVERY condition in all_of is true AND (any_of is empty OR at least one condition in any_of is true). hard_exclusion entries remove the item from DNA-scored results. combination entries apply a score penalty and never remove an item on their own.

hard_exclusion.note: Superhero structure is central. Not merely a powered character appearing.
Cinematic-universe-first storytelling. A standalone adaptation with an easter egg does not qualify.

combination.note: negative_signals #3, rewritten at MG-7.3. HIGH ACTION IS NOT THE PROBLEM. Space, military and sustained action are all fine when the title carries real Sci-Fi substance, so this fires only when scientific investigation AND rule discovery AND concept escalation AND mystery are all weak at the same time. A title with low literal scientific_investigation but strong rule discovery, mystery or concept escalation is doing Sci-Fi work by another route and is deliberately spared.
negative_signals #1. A high creature_threat alone is NOT penalised - an investigated organism is exactly what this profile wants.
negative_signals #2. High horror alone is NOT penalised.
negative_signals #4. Slow is not bad; slow WITHOUT discovery is.

not_expressible_in_dna.consumer_rule: NO CONSUMER MAY READ, EVALUATE OR SCORE THIS FIELD. It carries zero runtime semantics. It exists only to record that these two negative signals were considered and deliberately left out of the descriptive DNA vector, so that a future reader does not add dimensions for them by mistake. The DNA model is not required to encode every reason a title can be bad.

entries.signal: Sequel or remake that mostly repeats an already-seen concept without a substantial new idea
entries.reason: Already expressed by a low concept_escalation value under dna_baseline.weights. A separate penalty would double-count the same measurement.

entries.signal: Mystery whose payoff is primarily symbolic/ambiguous and not supported by ongoing discoveries
entries.reason: There is no payoff-quality DNA dimension and inventing one would be false precision. This remains a prose signal in negative_signals, interpreted by the automation at title level.

execution_preferences.description: Baseline POLICY for how execution evidence is applied. Policy only. Accumulated feedback is NEVER written here.
rules: Execution feedback never changes topic or DNA eligibility.
Concept feedback may refine content preference, conservatively and preferably on repeated independent evidence.
Tone feedback is a soft ranking adjustment and never a hard subject blacklist.
A single title never establishes a generalised content aversion.
Structured schema-2 feedback fields outrank speculative interpretation of free text.
The stable baseline remains dominant while feedback history is small.
